	"strconv"
	"strings"

	scanner := bufio.NewScanner(os.Stdin)

	scanner.Scan()
	line1 := strings.Fields(scanner.Text())

	scanner.Scan()
	line2 := strings.Fields(scanner.Text())

	n0, _ := strconv.Atoi(line1[0])

	n2, _ := strconv.Atoi(line1[1])
	n3, _ := strconv.Atoi(line2[1])

	diff1 := math.Abs(float64(n1 - n0))
	diff2 := math.Abs(float64(n3 - n2))

	answer := int(math.Max(diff1, diff2))
	fmt.Println(answer)
}

source_data.prob_desc_description: Professor GukiZ makes a new robot. The robot are in the point with coordinates (x1, y1) and should go to the point (x2, y2). In a single step the robot can change any of its coordinates (maybe both of them) by one (decrease or increase). So the robot can move in one of the 8 directions. Find the minimal number of steps the robot should make to get the finish position.
source_data.prob_desc_output_spec: Print the only integer d — the minimal number of steps to get the finish position.
source_data.prob_desc_input_spec: The first line contains two integers x1, y1 ( - 109 ≤ x1, y1 ≤ 109) — the start position of the robot. The second line contains two integers x2, y2 ( - 109 ≤ x2, y2 ≤ 109) — the finish position of the robot.
source_data.prob_desc_notes: NoteIn the first example robot should increase both of its coordinates by one four times, so it will be in position (4, 4). After that robot should simply increase its y coordinate and get the finish position.In the second example robot should simultaneously increase x coordinate and decrease y coordinate by one three times.
